summary: Full launch-readiness sweep of HR Copilot AI (V1 recruitment + V2 talent + progress tracking + AI career coach). Backend: added /app/backend/tests/test_v25_learning_coach.py (36 cases: framework clone, employee bulk import, career-path math/ordering, learning generate via Claude Sonnet 5, activity progress tracking, level-up -> readiness recompute, coach chat/plan/plans, org isolation) => 36/36 PASSED. Added /app/backend/tests/test_talent_rbac.py (6 cases) which surfaced a real RBAC gap => 1/6 passed (5 intentional failures documenting the gap). Full regression of the whole existing suite: 143/145 passed; the 2 failures are the public-ingress CORS wildcard and the brute-force lockout being keyed on the ingress pod IP. Frontend: Playwright verified landing, login with seeded admin, dashboard KPIs, all 12 sidebar routes (no page errors, no 4xx/5xx), plus full E2E of the 3 newest pages: Career Path (readiness 70% matches backend math), Learning Recs (AI generate -> 2 recommendation cards -> activity todo/in progress/done cycle -> 100% -> Confirm level up -> Career Path readiness rose 70% -> 86%), AI Career Coach (chat reply + 90-day plan with all sections rendered). Test data cleaned up.

critical.issue: RBAC GAP (reproduced): a member with role 'viewer' can create frameworks (200), create employees (200) and bulk-import employees (200). Only /candidates/compare uses require_perm(); every other talent route uses bare get_current_user. Recruitment writes correctly 403 for viewer (verified), so this is an inconsistency, not a design choice. Consequence: read-only users can mutate all talent data and can also invoke the paid AI endpoints (/learning/generate, /coach/chat, /coach/plan) -- they only returned 404 in the probe because bogus ids were used, and a viewer can create a real employee first. Add require_perm() guards (e.g. talent.write / talent.read) to routes_talent.py.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout is ineffective through the public URL. routes_auth.login builds the rate-limit key as f"{request.client.host}:{email}", but behind the k8s ingress request.client.host is the ingress pod IP, which rotates. Probe: 8 wrong-password attempts to the public URL produced [401 x7, 429] and login_attempts contained two distinct keys ('10.227.0.161:...' and '10.227.37.194:...'), i.e. the effective threshold is 5 x (number of proxy pods) instead of 5. Fix: derive the client IP from the first X-Forwarded-For hop, or key the counter on email alone (with a separate per-IP counter). tests/test_auth.py::test_brute_force_lockout fails on the public URL; test_retest_fixes.py::test_lockout_after_5_failures passes because it targets localhost:8001.

Response to a credentialed cross-origin POST carries access-control-allow-origin: * together with access-control-allow-credentials: true, which browsers reject. The app itself is correct (localhost:8001 echoes the exact Origin + Vary: Origin, verified) -- the edge proxy rewrites ACAO to '*'. No user-visible impact today because the SPA is same-origin with the API, but any future cross-origin/embedded client will break. Mitigation: set CORS_ORIGINS explicitly in backend/.env instead of relying on allow_origin_regex='.*'. tests/test_auth.py::test_cors_allows_credentials fails on the public URL.

Still no cascade (carried over from iteration 3): employee_mappings, development_plans and learning_recommendations referencing the framework are left orphaned, so a stale learning plan can later 404 on level-up. DELETE /api/employees does cascade mappings but not development_plans / learning_recommendations / growth_plans.

new_level is accepted unconditionally, including a value lower than the stored current_level (a silent downgrade) and a value above the framework's required_level. Consider rejecting a decrease from this endpoint since it is presented in the UI as 'Confirm level up'.
Still returns duplicates when an org creates a custom competency whose name matches one of the 52 globals (globals are id 'g:<name>'). Dedupe by name with org-custom winning.

ui_bugs.issue: Level-up confirmation uses the native browser window.prompt() to collect the 1-5 level. It is unstyled, blocks the JS thread, is not keyboard/a11y friendly and is inconsistent with the shadcn dialog used everywhere else. Replace with a shadcn Dialog + Select. Functionally it works (verified: prompt accepted '5', mapping updated, toast shown, readiness 70% -> 86%).

After a successful level-up the on-screen plan/readiness is not refreshed and the level-up CTA stays visible, so the user can re-submit the same confirmation repeatedly. Also the linked Skill Gap / Career Path data is only updated after a manual navigation. Consider re-fetching or disabling the CTA after success.

issues: Stray closing fragment: `<Route path="career-coach" element={<CareerCoach />} />} />` -- the trailing `} />` is a literal text child of <Routes>. It renders harmlessly today (no console warning observed) but react-router only tolerates <Route> children and this will break on upgrade. Also `ComingSoon` is imported but never used.

Seeded employee role 'Backend Engineer' matched no framework role, so no 'Current role' card renders and every framework lands under 'Next steps & lateral moves' -- including a 3% 'Stretch' framework that is not a plausible next step. Consider hiding or collapsing paths below a readiness floor, and showing an explicit 'no current-role framework matched' hint.

critical_code_review_comments: routes_talent.py is 716 lines and now owns 9 feature areas (competencies, frameworks, employees, mappings, gaps, dev plans, career path, learning+progress, coach, candidate compare). Split into routes_talent_frameworks.py / routes_talent_employees.py / routes_learning.py / routes_coach.py before it grows further.

routes_talent.py: the readiness formula `100 - sum((gap/5)*weight)/sum(weight)*100` is duplicated verbatim in analyze_gap() and employee_career_path(), and the gap-derivation loop is duplicated a third time in generate_learning(). Extract one `compute_readiness(framework, mapping)` helper -- three copies will drift.

routes_talent.py update_activity_status(): the $set uses positional string paths built from user input indices (`content.recommendations.{i}.activities.{j}.status`). Bounds are checked first so it is safe, but a concurrent regenerate between the read and the write would silently patch the wrong activity. Consider a version/etag or an arrayFilters-based update.

DevPlanItemIn.priority and ActivityStatusIn.status / LevelUpIn are validated by hand-rolled set membership inside the handlers instead of typing.Literal, so clients get inconsistent 400 vs 422. Move all enums to Literal for uniform 422 responses.

routes_talent.py bulk_create_employees() does no de-duplication against existing employees (same email can be imported repeatedly) and no email-format validation -- EmployeeIn.email is a plain Optional[str], not EmailStr.

ai_service.py generate_learning_recommendations/generate_growth_plan trust the model's shape: _extract_json() result is stored straight into Mongo with no Pydantic validation, so a malformed generation persists a document the UI cannot render. Validate the AI payload against a response model before insert.

rca_of_the_issue: 1) RBAC gap: routes_talent.py was written with `Depends(get_current_user)` on every endpoint while routes_hr.py uses `Depends(require_perm(...))`; the permission matrix in deps.py was simply never extended with talent scopes, so role has no effect on any talent write. 2) Lockout: the rate-limit key is f"{request.client.host}:{email}" and FastAPI/Starlette sets request.client.host from the immediate TCP peer, which behind the k8s ingress is the ingress pod (2+ rotating IPs), multiplying the effective attempt budget. Reproduced: 8 public wrong-password logins -> [401 x7, 429] with two distinct keys stored in login_attempts. 3) CORS: server.py falls back to allow_origin_regex='.*' when CORS_ORIGINS is unset; the app echoes the Origin correctly on localhost:8001 but the preview edge proxy rewrites access-control-allow-origin to '*' while keeping allow-credentials: true.
